first_impression.reaction: Arrived from a Google search for 'australia real wedding' while comparing planners. Jumped straight to the FAQ and the closing section looking for fees and budgets, found neither, then went back up. The intro is plain and doesn't oversell, which I'll give it. But 'Show me a real wedding with the actual budget' is exactly what I came for, and twelve couples with no cost, guest count or what the planner actually did is a mood board, not proof. I kept going mainly because the legal section looked like it had real sources.

journey.quote: Every Australia real wedding on this page comes from a story on our own pages: 12 couples, grouped by the setting they chose, whether that was a clifftop, a vineyard, a city room, a garden or an island.
journey.reaction: Fine, a straight description with a number. But 'from our own pages' doesn't tell me whether you planned any of these or just published them. That matters if this is meant to be proof of your work.

journey.quote: To marry legally in Australia, you give a Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.
journey.reaction: A concrete, checkable fact. I'll check it, but this is the kind of line I trust.

journey.section: Real weddings by the coast and beach
journey.quote: In Wollongong, Jennifer and Emrah exchanged vows on a clifftop beside the beach before moving on to a glamorous reception.
journey.reaction: 'Glamorous' tells me nothing. How many guests, what did it cost, what did the planner handle? Every card reads like this.

journey.quote: On a reef island, the water, the planting and the light arrive before a single flower is brought in.
journey.reaction: Pure atmosphere copy. Skimmed straight past it.

journey.quote: Each point below ends in questions to put to a venue before you sign, and the answers belong in writing.
journey.reaction: This is the most useful part for me. 'Get it in writing' is the right instinct and the question lists are practical.

journey.section: Styling that lets the setting lead
journey.quote: What can we bring in ourselves, and what has to come from the venue's own suppliers?
journey.reaction: Good question, but it stops short of the one I actually care about: are the venue's own suppliers marked up, and does anyone, including a planner, get paid a commission for steering me there?

journey.quote: As at November 2026, the Marriage Act 1961 and the Marriage Regulations 2017 set the rules for marrying in Australia.
journey.reaction: Dated, named legislation, a link to the government celebrant register, and 'not legal advice'. This is how you earn trust with me.

journey.quote: Bureau of Meteorology climate records for an island airport there show January and February far wetter, with many more days of rain, than late winter and early spring.
journey.reaction: Sourced and honest about a downside. Would prefer the actual numbers on the page rather than 'far wetter', but the link is there.

journey.section: Plan your Australian wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing up front is a genuine plus. But how is the fee worked out? Flat, percentage, or paid by the venues? 'Plans the payments' makes me more nervous, not less, if I can't see whether money passes through you with a margin on top.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor fee calculated: flat fee, percentage of spend, or something else?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or referral fee from venues or vendors it recommends?
Are supplier prices passed through at cost, or with a mark-up?
Did Wedded Wonderland plan any of these 12 weddings, or are they published stories only?
What did any of these weddings roughly cost, and how many guests did they have?
What exactly is included in the fee, and what costs extra?
Are there independent reviews of the Wedded Concierge service, and where?

turn_offs_found.quote: In Wollongong, Jennifer and Emrah exchanged vows on a clifftop beside the beach before moving on to a glamorous reception.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional description instead of facts. No budget, guest count or scope on any card.

turn_offs_found.quote: Near the Gold Coast, Samira and Tom married beneath a handcrafted arch set against a green garden, a look that felt polished and unhurried at once.
turn_offs_found.why: Feelings, not information. I can't compare this to anything.

turn_offs_found.quote: Take them to every site visit, and to your first conversation with Wedded Concierge.
turn_offs_found.why: A link to the sales page halfway down, before I've seen anything about how you're paid. Mild, but noticed.

would_share_with: My partner, for the venue question lists and the legal section only

cta_reaction.quote: Share with Wedded Concierge the setting you picture, the month you are weighing, your guest numbers and how far everyone will travel.
cta_reaction.why: The questions are sensible and the 'fee agreed in writing' line helps. But I'd only enquire after I've found your fee model and commission policy somewhere else on the site. This page asks me to hand over my details without telling me what I'm paying for or who else is paying you.

top_3_changes: Add supplier mark-up and commission questions to the styling checklist so the page shows it isn't afraid of the money question (exact edit in suggested_edits[0]).
Be upfront in the intro that the cards cover settings, not costs, so a reader looking for budgets isn't left feeling misled (exact edit in suggested_edits[1]).
Cut the atmosphere line on the island section and replace it with a plain lead-in using facts already on the page (exact edit in suggested_edits[2]).

suggested_edits.old: - What can we bring in ourselves, and what has to come from the venue's own suppliers?
suggested_edits.new:
- What can we bring in ourselves, and what has to come from the venue's own suppliers?
- If we use the venue's own suppliers, can we see their prices itemised in writing?
- Does the venue pay a commission to any planner or agent who refers couples?
suggested_edits.rationale: Adds reader-side questions only, no new facts. Signals honesty about money, which is my top trust signal.

suggested_edits.old: Each card links to the couple's full story.
suggested_edits.new: Each card links to the couple's full story. The cards describe the setting each couple chose, not what their wedding cost.
suggested_edits.rationale: States a limitation of this page itself. No new facts about the weddings or the business.

suggested_edits.old: On a reef island, the water, the planting and the light arrive before a single flower is brought in.
suggested_edits.new: One couple here married on an island in the Whitsundays.
suggested_edits.rationale: Replaces emotional filler with a plain line restating what the card below already says.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel the sceptic (fees, commissions, proof first)
No invented brand facts; fee model and commission policy listed as unanswered
Read only the persona card, draft and schema
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored as invisible
Suggested edits (max 3) add no prices, venue or vendor names, statistics, business details or new real-wedding facts

assumptions: Arrived via a Google search for the primary keyword 'australia real wedding' while comparing planners.
Read FAQ and closing section first, per decision_behaviour, then the rest of the page.

open_questions.question: Is there an approved, published statement of the Wedded Advisor fee model and commission policy that a later stage could link to from this post? Without it, this persona will not enquire from this page.
Did Wedded Wonderland plan any of the featured weddings? If so, can the source stories confirm it so the page can say so?
